solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Locate vision in speech (4)

indicators.note: what is said rather than written, so the sound counts

annotation.surface: Someone trying to pin down a vision described in a speech.
annotation.walkthrough: SITE is a verb here, as in siting a new factory, so it swaps cleanly for 'Locate'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym, as when planners choose where a new school should go.

clue.text: Curved structure over motorway in spot I don’t know (6,2)

indicators.note: the arch and motorway go inside the word for spot

blocks.note: an arch is a curved structure
M = motorway, as in the M1; 'over' puts it after ARCH in this down clue

annotation.surface: A bridge arching over a motorway, described by someone who has no idea where it is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is the verb, to see, not a place; ARCH and M sit between its two E's.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Search me' is a shrugging way of saying I don't know.

clue.text: Instruction to express impatience with delay in middle of speech (8)

indicators.note: LAG goes inside the middle letters
take the central letters of 'speech'

blocks.note: tut is the sound of impatience
the two central letters of sPEECh

annotation.surface: A speaker being told to tut at a hold-up halfway through a speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speech' has an even number of letters, so its middle is two letters rather than one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means guardianship and the teaching given under it.

clue.text: Almost admit, on reflection, act involving bad misdemeanour (10)

indicators.note: 'Almost' means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short.
a reflection turns it back to front
'Involving' means taking in, so the word for act takes the word for bad inside it.

annotation.surface: Someone half-owning up to wrongdoing as they look back on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like hindsight but turns the shortened word round; the whole surface is a confession, which suits the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Spanish for 'little sin': a small, forgivable fault.

clue.text: Guarantee yielding right result (5)

indicators.note: giving up, so the R is surrendered

annotation.surface: A promise that a correct outcome will follow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Result' is the verb here, to follow as a consequence, matching the verb ENSUE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to follow on as a consequence of something.

clue.text: Cleaner, left in muddle, having no appeal (9)

indicators.note: 'In' puts one thing inside another: 'left in muddle' means L sitting within the word for muddle.

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning lady

annotation.surface: A cleaner who left things in a mess and so has lost all appeal.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a char is a hired house cleaner; L goes inside MESS after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Charmless means lacking any appeal.

clue.text: Estimation of position that’s insensitive about country’s leader, monarch carrying on (4,9)

indicators.note: the first letter of 'country's'
'Carrying' means bearing something within, so the monarch carries the word 'on' inside him.

blocks.note: the word itself, carried inside KING

annotation.surface: A tactless comment about a nation's leader while the king carries on regardless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' splits: 'carrying' is the instruction and 'on' is the letters KING holds.
annotation.definitionFit: Dead reckoning is working out a ship's position from speed, heading and time, without landmarks.

clue.text: Seed, one ending in final, fast getting on top (6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'final'
in a down clue, LENT goes above the rest

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter

annotation.surface: A seed that was one of the finalists, with a quick one leading.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is not speed but the religious fast, Lent, which sits on top of I and L.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the small lens-shaped pulse is the dried seed of a legume.

clue.text: Start unfashionable group (6)

annotation.surface: Forming a group of people who are not in style.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start' reads as a verb but is the noun, the beginning.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: the very beginning, as in 'from the word go'.

clue.text: While around river, one encountered retiring goddess (7)

indicators.note: 'Around' means encircling, so the word for while wraps round the letters that follow.
going back, so I MET reverses

annotation.surface: A shy goddess met by someone on the way round a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a shy description of the goddess; it turns I MET round to TEMI.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: she is the Greek huntress, twin of Apollo.

clue.text: Crafty chap, evil animal, badly wanting power (13)

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, so rearrange them
'Wanting' means lacking, so the chap is left without the letter for power.

blocks.note: CHAP with its last letter, P, removed, as 'wanting power' asks

annotation.surface: A wily man and a wicked beast, both short on strength.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crafty chap' reads as one phrase, but only 'Crafty' is the definition and 'chap' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Machiavellian means cunning and scheming, after Machiavelli.

clue.text: Opposing commander isn’t worried (7)

indicators.note: letters worried out of shape

blocks.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander
the letters of ISNT, anagram fodder

annotation.surface: The enemy general is not anxious.
annotation.walkthrough: AGA is an old Turkish title for a military commander, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe standing on the other side, as when voting no.

clue.text: Cleanser in middle of kitchen getting on with stuff, filled with energy (4,5)

indicators.note: the central letter of 'kitchen'
'Filled with' means having something put inside, so the word for stuff holds E.

blocks.note: the fourth of seven letters in kitCHen

annotation.surface: Someone in the kitchen getting on with their cleaning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' is not carrying on but getting old.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an oily cream rubbed on and wiped off to lift make-up and dirt.

clue.text: Put up orator’s level (5)

indicators.note: as a speaker says it, so go by sound

blocks.note: to raze = to level to the ground

annotation.surface: A speaker's podium being set higher.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that raze and raise sound alike but mean opposite things: flatten and build up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean build or hoist, as with a barn or a flag.

clue.text: Superb quality in publication with good binding provided by New Church (12)

indicators.note: 'Binding' means wrapping round and holding together, so the word for good wraps round the word for provided.

annotation.surface: Praise for a finely bound magazine produced by a new church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Binding' suggests bookbinding and 'New Church' a congregation, but they are an instruction and two abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grandeur or splendour, the noun for being superb.

clue.text: Not even unusual urge stops terrible liar, traitor ultimately (9)

indicators.note: the letters of 'urge' in an unusual order
plugs a gap, so goes inside
the letters of 'liar' made a mess of
the last letter of 'traitor'

blocks.note: anagram of LIAR, split by REGU

annotation.surface: A strange compulsion halts a dreadful liar and, in the end, a traitor.
annotation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams are at work, each with its own indicator, and one ends up inside the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: uneven, as in a jagged edge or an unsteady pulse.

clue.text: Airy editor’s opening article, authentic (8)

indicators.note: the first letter of 'editor's'

annotation.surface: An editor's breezy front-page piece that rings true.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening article' reads as an editorial; it splits into E and THE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: delicate and light, as if made of the upper air, the ether.

clue.text: It’s drunk, otherwise it’s eaten (8)

indicators.note: in another way, so rearrange

annotation.surface: A riddle about something swallowed as drink or else as food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It's drunk' looks like an anagram indicator on 'it's'; it is the definition, a liqueur you drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed liqueur, so something drunk.

clue.text: European with jolly temper receiving love periodically (5,2,5)

indicators.note: 'Receiving' means taking in, so the word for temper takes love inside it.

blocks.note: jolly = very, as in jolly good

annotation.surface: A cheerful but hot-tempered European who is sometimes shown love.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' and 'temper' look like moods; in Britain 'jolly' is also an adverb meaning very, and 'temper' is the verb soften.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for at intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Pursued by police, rushed off (6)

indicators.note: 'Pursued by' means chased, so the police come behind the word for rushed.

blocks.note: CID is the British police detective branch

annotation.surface: Someone chased by the police who ran away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rushed off' looks like one phrase; 'off' is the definition, as food goes off.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Off' in the sense of spoiled food: butter or oil that has turned and smells sour.

clue.text: Odds linked to place on ladder jumped (6)

blocks.note: SP = starting price, the odds on a horse at the off
a rung is a step on a ladder

annotation.surface: The betting odds depend on how high up the ladder you stand.
annotation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is British racing shorthand for the odds when a race begins.
annotation.definitionFit: Sprung is a past tense of spring, to jump.

clue.text: Shock assistant, turning against crony (5)

indicators.note: 'Turning' means facing the other way, so the assistant is written back to front.

blocks.note: a pal is a friend or crony

annotation.surface: An assistant shocks everyone by turning on a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Against' here just sets AP beside PAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to horrify or dismay someone.

clue.text: Piety in turn followed by rows between daughter and son (9)

indicators.note: GO comes first, the rest after
LINES sits between D and S

annotation.surface: Churchgoers taking turns, the family seated in rows between daughter and son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rows' sounds like arguments between the children; it means lines.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: devoutness, living as God would wish.

clue.text: Storehouse in spot holding record (5)

indicators.note: 'Holding' means gripping from outside, so the spot keeps the record inside it.

blocks.note: an EP, extended play, is a record

annotation.surface: A warehouse in a particular spot where records are kept.
annotation.walkthrough: EP is a short vinyl record, longer than a single.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a warehouse, or a yard where buses or goods are kept.

clue.text: Spies in constant control endlessly essential (7)

indicators.note: 'In' places the spies inside the letters for constant and control.
RULE loses its last letter

blocks.note: C = the speed of light, a constant

annotation.surface: Spies under constant control are said to be vital.
annotation.walkthrough: C is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light, a constant; CIA goes inside C + RUL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vital, the thing everything else depends on.

clue.text: Paint holy man taking Mass (7)

indicators.note: 'Taking' means taking in, so the man absorbs the letter for Mass.

annotation.surface: A painting of a priest at Mass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holy man' looks like one unit, a saint; it is PI + GENT, and 'Mass' is the physics M, not the church service.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: colouring matter, which mixed with a binder makes paint.

clue.text: Decline, for example, going into retreat ending in terrible cost (10)

indicators.note: 'Going into' means entering, so 'for example' enters the retreat.
the last letter of 'terrible'

blocks.note: a den is a private retreat
a rate = a cost or charge

annotation.surface: An army retreating at terrible cost, its fortunes in decline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' is the noun, a den, not the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to deteriorate, sinking to a worse state.

clue.text: Delight in jungle expedition (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words

annotation.surface: Joy on a jungle trek.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters run across the word break, jungLE Expedition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: joy, high spirits.
